title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: answers draw on images embedded in Word, PowerPoint and PDF files
summary: The roadmap facts, control paths and PowerShell command are supported, and searches did not find an image-reading switch or feature-specific licensing. The briefing should not assert that the earlier uploaded-image capability is a different feature without evidence, and should acknowledge Microsoft's conflicting guidance about blocking Copilot in Teams.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The app-blocking path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Block app.
claims.quote:
Select Settings, and then select Integrated Apps.
Select the Available Apps list.
Select an app from the Available Apps list to open the overview pane.
Select Block app.

claims.where: controls[0].governs and note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Integrated Apps Copilot app control affects both Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat, rather than image reading alone.
claims.quote: On the Integrated Apps page, the CoPilot app settings apply to both Microsoft Copilot and the Copilot Chat apps. Any changes made to this app from the integrated apps portal apply to both.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls

In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites.
Select the site you want to configure.
Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.
